skills.title: Bringing a Meegle work item into Cadence
skills.whenToUse: Before turning anything from list_work_items into a Cadence task — the list needs judging before it is copied.
skills.body:
list_work_items returns what Meegle has assigned to this person. It is a queue, not a plan, and most of it should not become a task.

Judge the list before copying any of it:

1. `alreadyInCadence: true` means a task already stands for it. Leave it alone. Creating another is the failure this whole path is designed around.
2. A `state` of RESOLVED, CLOSED or similar means the item is finished even though it is still listed. Do not bring it across.
3. A fresh Meegle space is seeded with onboarding cards — "Welcome to Meegle", "Create a space", "Invite a team member". They are documentation wearing the shape of work. If a space's whole list looks like a product tour, it probably is one; say so rather than importing it.
4. What is left is real. Bring across only what matters in the period being planned, and say in `explain` which ones and why. Everything you import is something the user will later find in their list and have to place.

Writing the task:

- **A ticket title names a symptom; a task title names an action.** "User cannot log-in" is a report. "Reproduce the login failure" is a task. Write what the user would have written if they had typed it themselves.
- Keep the ticket's own wording in `notes`, so the original is not lost in the rewrite.
- Pass `externalID` through exactly as given. It is what makes a later sync revise this task instead of creating a second copy of it.
- Do not invent an estimate. Call `get_estimate_history` first; if there is nothing comparable, propose a short block to scope the work rather than a long one to do it — a 30-minute block that ends in a real estimate beats a three-hour guess.

Dates:

Most work items carry no schedule at all — the `schedule` object comes back with empty strings rather than nulls. That is not missing data. Meegle says what has to be done; deciding when is the reason Cadence exists. Use `find_free_slots`.

If a work item does have dates, treat them as the team's expectation rather than the user's own due date, and say so if the two disagree.
